answers.answer: During London Season attrition, simultaneously roll one die for each held office card. Add one for each fatigue on that card, and add one extra for the Chairman. A modified result of 1–2 has no effect; 3–4 adds fatigue; 5 or more retires the officeholder: move the member to Pensioners, flip the card to Vacant Offices, and return its fatigue to supply. Commanders have no office card and do not roll normal office attrition.
answers.evidence: London Season—Attrition: office die plus fatigue; Chairman also adds one; 1–2 nothing, 3–4 fatigue, 5+ retire; retiree to Pensioners, card to Vacant Offices, fatigue to supply.

answers.answer: Only players who retired at least one pensioner may take or discard one card from the London Season display. They act in descending order of their actual total retirement spending. Ties go to the player with the most total windows, counting new prizes, then clockwise from the Prime Minister. The acting player may peek at display blackmails. Do not replace cards during selection; if the display empties, skip all remaining eligible players immediately. After the selection step, discard every card still displayed and refill exactly three cards—prestige faceup and blackmail facedown—even if nobody took a card. Return unused pensioners to their supplies.
answers.evidence: London Season—Prestige: eligible retirees, descending actual spending; ties by windows then clockwise from PM; no replacement; empty display skips; discard and refill exactly three; return unused Pensioners.

answers.answer: At the start of a player's Family action, check where their opportunity marker was at phase start. They may take their chosen main action twice if the marker already matched that action; otherwise they take it once. They then move the marker onto the chosen main action. Only the latest passed extra-action law may grant a later extra action; that action is never doubled by the marker and does not move it. If at least four offices are vacant, Enlist Writer places one additional writer once that turn, including when the main action is doubled. Thus if the marker is already on Enlist Writer and four offices are vacant, the player may place three writers total (two from the doubled action plus the one-time bonus).
answers.evidence: Family steps 1–4; Enlist Writer: with at least four vacant offices place one additional writer once this turn, so doubled action can place three total.

answers.answer: After all players finish Family actions, while both Company Debt and applicants remain, move the rightmost Stock Exchange applicant into Court and lower Debt by one; repeat while both Debt and applicants remain. Court pieces are Company shares. If there is no Debt, slide remaining applicants as far right as possible while preserving their order. Seeking a share pays its listed purchase cost to the bank; it does not pay family cash into Company treasuries. The summary does not state a different destination for that initial purchase money, so the destination beyond payment to the bank is unsupported.
answers.evidence: Family—Seek Share: pay bank; applicant, not yet share. New Company shares: rightmost applicant to Court while Debt remains; lower Debt; with no Debt slide applicants right; seeking never pays family cash into Company treasuries.

answers.answer: Fill vacant offices in ascending order of the number on their office-card backs. The designated hirer chooses a candidate and moves that family member into the office; the member's owner receives the office card. Promoting an officeholder transfers that office's fatigue to the new card and inserts the old card, now vacant, into the ascending hiring order. An ordinary hire of your own family requires verbal consent from every other player represented in that office's candidate pool; Chairman elections and Commander appointments are exempt. If no candidate exists, or the designated hirer is vacant, skip the office: it remains vacant and takes no actions, including hiring. The summary does not state any further special procedure for a case with no candidate or hirer.
answers.evidence: Hiring: ascending card-back order, fatigue follows promotion, old card re-enters order; skip if no candidate or hirer. Nepotism requires every other represented candidate-pool player’s consent, with stated exemptions.

answers.answer: The former Chairman first announces how many shares are needed for a pure majority, meaning more than half of the current shares. Any shareholder may campaign; the first candidate supported by players controlling that many shares wins. Move one of the winner's Company shares to the Chairman slot and give them the title marker. If nobody receives majority support, the former Chairman chooses any shareholder, including themself, without Nepotism consent. If the Court is empty, the former Chairman automatically returns; place a member from supply, or if necessary and possible take one from a prize and lose that prize's VP. If that cannot be done, there is no Chairman. The elected Chairman piece remains a Company share for dividends, majority calculations and scoring, but it cannot be traded or invested in a firm.
answers.evidence: Chairman election: announce pure majority; first supported candidate wins; no-support fallback; empty Court fallback; Chairman share counts for dividends/majority/scoring but cannot be traded or invested.

answers.answer: For a Company-office success check, first commit resources and any cash; all cash comes from that acting office's treasury and is paid to the bank. Gather dice, subtract penalties, and roll. Use the lowest die: 1–2 succeeds; 3–4 fails and may be retried if resources and office-specific limits allow; 5–6 is catastrophic failure, ending that office's actions, returning its officeholder to supply, discarding fatigue, and flipping its card into Vacant Offices. Specific Commander and firm procedures can modify this procedure. Do not take a dead action with no effect or chance of success; examples are trading with no ship or deploying without dice just to trigger possible officer losses.
answers.evidence: Success checks: office treasury cash paid to bank; lowest die 1–2 success, 3–4 failure/retry if allowed, 5–6 catastrophe and office removal; no dead actions.

answers.answer: The Chairman may voluntarily add up to three Debt, receiving £5 Balance for each, without consent. Each additional advance requires consent from players controlling a majority of Company shares, counting the Chairman, and Debt may never pass the end of its track. The Chairman must then allocate all Balance to other offices' treasuries, reducing Balance by the amount transferred. Borrowing and allocation may be interleaved, provided the total borrowing follows those limits. Cash already in office treasuries remains there for those offices to use.
answers.evidence: Chairman: up to three Debt freely at £5 Balance each; further advances need majority-share consent; do not pass Debt track end; allocate all Balance to other offices; may interleave.

answers.answer: The Manager of Shipping must spend from the office treasury until £2 or less remains. They may lease an extra ship for £2, fit a ship from a shipyard for £3 without the shipyard owner's consent, or buy a Company ship for £5 only if no ships remain on shipyards. Each acquired ship may be placed in any sea zone, including China once that office exists. Leased extra ships last only until Refresh. The summary does not specify an additional consent requirement for these Shipping purchases; fitting explicitly needs none. The separate firm rule says fitting a ship for a firm costs £3 from its London treasury and requires the shipyard owner's consent, and a firm may buy a player-owned ship already in Company only with owner consent (unfatigued £3 or fatigued £2, paid into Shipping treasury); firms cannot acquire Company or extra ships.
answers.evidence: Manager of Shipping: must spend to £2 or less; lease £2, fit £3 without owner consent, buy Company ship £5 only if no ships on shipyards; any sea zone; extra ships through Refresh. Firm ship rules also stated.

answers.answer: A President declares the regions for a Trade attempt, including its home region and only regions reachable through open orders with available ship capacity. Each £1 in the President's treasury buys one die; subtract one die for each declared nonhome region. On success, fill one order per ship in that sea zone, as many as possible within the declared regions: the first writer goes to the home port, and each following order must be adjacent to an order already filled by that Presidency. Use actual writers while available, then filled-order tokens. A President cannot fill another President's home region even if that President's office is vacant. If writers are insufficient, the summary directs use of filled-order tokens after available writers, so filling can continue. Increase Company Balance by each order's printed value, or half rounded down if a firm already filled that order this turn under deregulation. The President gets £1 from the bank per order and each writer owner gets £1 per writer placed. Each President can have at most one successful Trade per turn. A failed attempt/retry remains that President's uninterrupted opportunity; no other position may act between its attempts.
answers.evidence: Presidency operations: declared regions, £1 per die and nonhome penalty; order adjacency/capacity, writers then tokens, protected home regions, revenue and bonuses, one successful Trade.

answers.answer: A Commander may target their own Presidency's home region, any region associated with that Presidency, or any region bordering an associated region. They cannot target another Presidency's home region or another Presidency's Company-controlled region. A Company region is a valid target only if it has unrest or a closed order, so the action can have an effect. Exhaust chosen officers and regiments for one die each, and local alliances for their printed dice; subtract the combined strength of the target and all other regions in its empire, counting the target only once. Company-controlled defense strength is zero. A noncatastrophic failure may be retried using remaining resources. After every attempt, owners roll one die per officer exhausted in that attempt; each 6 returns that officer to supply. Regiments do not roll officer-loss dice. Each local alliance's strength is usable only once that turn, for Deploy or defense, and cannot be split between them.
answers.evidence: Commanders and Deploy: targets and restrictions; Company target effect condition; dice and empire penalty; post-attempt officer-loss rolls; alliances once per turn.

answers.answer: On a successful Deploy, take loot from the bank equal to £4 per tower in the target plus its faceup loot modifier, with a minimum of the number of surviving officers used in that attempt plus £1. Count only surviving participating officers and the regiments/alliance pieces used in that attempt. Distribute each £1 in repeated cycles, stopping when loot runs out: first £1 for the Commander plus £1 for each of the Commander's used surviving officers; then £1 per used surviving officer belonging to other families in clockwise order; then £1 per used regiment and per local-alliance piece to the bank. Repeat the cycle from the Commander until all loot is distributed. The Commander also takes one trophy per target tower. Then remove the target tower/dome, remove all matching empire flags if it was a capital, open all its orders and clear unrest. If the Elephant in the conquered region pointed outward, put it fully inside that region for Rebellion. On catastrophe, return half the Commander's family's trophies rounded up, return the Commander member to supply, and still check losses for the officers exhausted in the attempt; a Commander has no office card to vacate.
answers.evidence: Deploy success: loot formula/minimum and repeated payout cycle, trophies and control changes; catastrophe trophy return, Commander removal, and officer loss checks.

answers.answer: A Governor takes the printed dice pool. Each Administer attempt rolls the current pool with no penalty, then reduces the pool by one regardless of the result. On success the Governor takes £1, or £2 if the immediately preceding roll was unsuccessful, then chooses exactly one benefit: build a Company ship, commission a regiment, or tax. Building requires two successful Build actions: if there is no ship in the region, put a partially built Company ship there; otherwise complete that ship into the sea zone associated with the Governor's President. A commissioned regiment goes into the Army associated with that President. Tax adds an unsplit £2 to Company Balance or that President's treasury; each Tax after the first this turn adds unrest in the region. Any unsuccessful roll adds one unrest there; catastrophe also removes the officeholder under the normal rule. Repeat with the shrinking pool until the Governor stops, has no dice remaining, or catastrophically fails.
answers.evidence: Governors—Administer: shrinking pool regardless of result; success income and one benefit; build/regiment/tax details; unsuccessful unrest and catastrophe; stopping conditions.

answers.answer: Company expenses reduce Balance by £1 for each existing Debt, each officer or regiment in an Army, and each ship in sea zones, including China; Commanders are excluded. If Balance cannot cover expenses, take £5 emergency loans, increasing Debt by one per loan until the Debt track ends, and continue taking loans even at maximum Debt. Newly added emergency Debt causes no extra expense this turn. After the loans, set Balance to zero. One or two loans lower Standing one space; three or more lower it two. Then compare the remaining Balance with the expectations at current Standing; if it is lower, decrease Standing one. Finally, the Chairman may pay any affordable number of dividends: each costs £1 per Company share and pays £1 to each share owner, including the Chairman. If total cash paid in dividends is strictly greater than expectations, increase Standing one. The summary describes these checks in this order: expenses/emergency loans, expectations, then dividends.
answers.evidence: Revenue: expenses and emergency loans including max-Debt and Standing effects; expectations under current Standing; dividends and strict-greater-than increase.

answers.answer: A Crisis occurs at the Elephant's location, with its tail as attacker and head as target, then the Elephant marches. For a sovereign Invasion, compare the attacking empire's total strength plus event modifier against the defending empire's total strength; the attacker must be strictly greater. On success the defender's flag is replaced, and taking a capital shatters its whole empire; on failure the attacker loses one tower. For Rebellion, compare only the rebelling region's strength plus modifier against its sovereign capital's strength, strictly greater to succeed; other empire regions do not count. Success makes the actor sovereign, removes its flag and closes its orders; failure removes one tower from the capital. If the target is a Company region, the primary Invasion or Rebellion also triggers secondary Rebellions in every other Company region with unrest. Resolve the primary first, then secondary regions in Bombay, Madras, Bengal order, with each Commander ordering attacks within their Presidency. Primary normal Crisis strength is ordinary Invasion/Rebellion strength plus target unrest; primary Foreign Invasion uses its ordinary die without added unrest; each secondary Rebellion uses only unrest in that region. The associated Commander exhausts active Army pieces totaling the attack strength or as much as possible, using alliance strength without splitting it. Insufficient newly exhausted defense strength causes Region Loss. Sufficient defense removes all unrest and gives the Commander a trophy; if it successfully defended against a normal primary Invasion, also remove one tower from the attacking region if possible. If Commander is vacant, Military Affairs acts, or Chairman if that office is vacant; that acting player chooses defense pieces and gains/loses no trophies. A successful Company-targeting primary Invasion also applies empire growth.
answers.evidence: Events—Crisis/Invasion/Rebellion and Attacks on Company: primary and secondary regions/order/strength, defense pieces, insufficient/sufficient defense, vacant Commander procedure.

answers.answer: During ordinary law resolution, support of −1 or less means failure: discard the law; resolve a dilemma's If Failed text; the Opposition Leader returns the token and takes the Prime Minister dial; the new PM moves the proposed policy one space in either direction and resolves that adjacent policy. Support of zero or higher passes: place the law among passed laws, the PM takes a passed-law token, resolve the selected policy first, then the law's immediate effects. Restore all cards used for voting to their regular orientation after either result. If the law causes Company failure, finish the vote before Final Scoring. The summary also says the PM may call another full voting round or stop after each; a round with no votes must end voting.
answers.evidence: Parliament—Voting/Resolution: -1 or less fails with PM succession and policy shift; zero or higher passes with policy before immediate effects; reset cards after either.

answers.answer: In the 1758 and Long 1710 scenarios, at the start of a turn before London Season, the PM may call the special Deregulation vote if Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, and must call it if either is on a starred space. On passing, lower Debt by one per two current Debt, set Standing to S, give the PM a passed-law token, and activate firms. On failure, increase Company-share scoring value by flipping/placing the Court VP token, to a maximum of ±3. This special vote has no policy. A failed vote does not remove the PM and does not discard the Deregulation law; the PM may vote against it. The 1813 scenario begins deregulated. The summary gives no such call procedure for 1710 itself, except Long 1710; other ordinary-voting rules are not said to apply to this special vote beyond the stated PM ability to vote against.
answers.evidence: Deregulation: 1758/Long 1710 timing and optional/mandatory trigger; pass/failure effects; no policy; PM retained and law not discarded; 1813 starts deregulated.

answers.answer: To form a firm, a player must currently manage no firm and contribute either an eligible Company share returned to supply or a workshop flipped to its invested side. Flip the family board, place a family member as the first firm share, set Value to the leftmost track space, and take £5 from the bank into the firm's London treasury. To invest in an existing firm, get the manager's consent and contribute the same type of Company share or workshop; each investment takes £5 from the bank into London and creates a firm share until the firm has ten. Contributions beyond ten shares still add £5 but create no shares. The Chairman share cannot be used; no Company shares may be invested when Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space; shares created this turn cannot be used, even if traded away. A firm share contribution cannot be a share that was just created this turn. Family cash cannot be moved into or out of firm treasuries except through specified procedures. An invested workshop never returns to its uninvested side and gives neither the normal workshop bonus nor VP upon Company failure; it stays invested even if the firm fails. The summary does not separately define which Company shares are eligible beyond these restrictions.
answers.evidence: Firms phase—Form/Invest: share or workshop contribution; £5 from bank to London; manager consent, ten-share cap, Chairman/lined/this-turn restrictions; invested workshops remain so.

answers.answer: Each firm receives exactly one trade attempt per turn. Managers secretly and simultaneously choose a trade zone/home port or Hobnob; a trade choice requires at least one ship and commits a secret cash bid from London, while a closed home port is allowed when choosing. Hobnob makes no bid, trade, or dividend, but still pays expenses and retains its previous dividend marker. Reveal bids simultaneously; strategy cards stay facedown until the matching Presidency begins. At the start of that Presidency's operations, before any actions, matching firms reveal and roll one die per committed £1, paying the bid to the bank. At least one 1 or 2 allows the firm to trade. Initiative is ship count minus successful bid dice (1s/2s), possibly negative. A President's successful Trade creates initiative similarly using Presidency ships. After that President succeeds, fill in lowest-initiative order; the President chooses order among ties, so Company is not automatically first. If the President is vacant or never successfully Trades, firms fill after Commander/Governor opportunities, and the Chairman breaks initiative ties. A firm fills open orders up to ships plus one, starting at its chosen home port and tracing through its own filled route back to it; it fills each order at most once. Firms may refill an order filled earlier that turn by another firm or Company, and Company may refill a firm's order. A previously filled order pays half listed revenue rounded down. Trade revenue goes to India treasury; increase firm Value one space per full £6 added to India treasury that turn.
answers.evidence: Firm strategies/competing trade: eligibility, bidding and checks, reveal timing, initiative/ties, order capacity/routes/repeats, half revenue and value advancement.

answers.answer: At the start of Revenue, before the Company, firms pay expenses in initiative order, then other firms; ties are resolved by the manager with the most windows, then PM-clockwise order. Expenses are £1 per charter ship plus the higher of the firm's share count or Value, payable from either or both firm treasuries. If unable to pay, the firm dissolves unless rescued. Dissolution sends shares to Debtor's Prison (−1 VP each), returns ships to shipyards, returns the charter to its family side, and leaves workshops invested. Rescue can use emergency investments under normal share/workshop rules: pay expenses, lose remaining cash, and lower Value one space per emergency investment, even if the ten-share cap prevents more shares. Alternatively the firm may merge with one other firm; that firm must first pay its own expenses if not already paid, then cover the endangered firm's unpaid expenses. After expenses, the manager may pay dividends only from India treasury; each dividend costs £1 per firm share plus £1 for the manager. With manager consent, a shareholder may forgo payment for any number of their shares on any dividend. Record the total actual cash paid out—not a per-share dividend—with the dividend cube on the Company Balance track. An active non-Hobnob firm that pays nothing records zero; Hobnob retains its previous marker. Sweep remaining India money into London. Firm ships are exposed to storms in their strategy zone; Hobnob ships are exempt.
answers.evidence: Firm expenses/rescue/dividends: expense calculation and treasury sources; failure/dissolution and rescue routes; dividend calculation, recording, sweep and storm exposure.
